name: Space Exploration
description: Space travel from the first rockets and the race to the Moon to space stations, rovers on Mars and the reusable rockets of today.

checkpoints.name: The first rockets
checkpoints.note: Goddard flies the first liquid-fuelled rocket in 1926. Germany's V-2 reaches space in war, and afterwards its engineers build rockets for both the United States and the Soviet Union.

checkpoints.name: Sputnik and the first people in space
checkpoints.note: The Soviet Union launches Sputnik in 1957 and sends Laika, then Yuri Gagarin and Valentina Tereshkova, into orbit. The United States answers with Mercury, Gemini and a promise to reach the Moon.

checkpoints.name: The Moon landing
checkpoints.note: Apollo recovers from a deadly fire. In July 1969 Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walk on the Moon, and twelve people walk there before Apollo ends in 1972.

checkpoints.name: Stations and shuttles
checkpoints.note: Skylab and the Soviet Salyut and Mir stations keep people in orbit for months. The Space Shuttle flies for thirty years, and the Hubble Space Telescope is launched.

checkpoints.name: The space station years
checkpoints.note: Former rivals build the International Space Station together. China sends its first astronaut, and rovers begin to explore Mars.

checkpoints.name: Rovers and reusable rockets
checkpoints.note: SpaceX lands and reuses rockets and flies crews to the station. China builds its own station and lands on the far side of the Moon, rovers search Mars for signs of life, and Artemis aims to take people back to the Moon.
